profile.campus: Clarksville-Montgomery County, Tennessee (Google's Boolean Drive / Jim Johnson Road campus)
profile.address: Boolean Drive, Montgomery County, Middle Tennessee, Tennessee
profile.reading: This building, tagged SPC1A in OpenStreetMap, was the first phase of Google's Clarksville-Montgomery County data center campus, the company's first data center in Tennessee. Google, the Tennessee Valley Authority, and Governor Bill Haslam's administration announced the roughly $600 million project through the Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development, and Google formally opened the facility on November 6, 2019, in a ribbon-cutting ceremony led by then-Governor Bill Lee, following a construction start in February 2018. The campus draws power in part through a 413-megawatt renewable energy purchase agreement Google struck with the Tennessee Valley Authority, sourced from solar farms totaling roughly 1.6 million panels across sites in Tennessee and Alabama, one of the larger corporate renewable power deals TVA has signed. Google has said it gave more than $450,000 to local nonprofits and schools in the Clarksville area in the years following the data center's opening, part of a broader community-investment pattern the company has repeated at other US data center sites. Since construction began in 2018, Google reports investing more than $6 billion in Tennessee overall, a figure that under its updated economic-impact methodology includes data center construction along with server and networking capital expenditure rather than construction costs alone, and the company says it helped generate $11.4 billion of economic activity for Tennessee businesses, nonprofits, and developers in 2025. Google's data center locations page and its economic-impact reporting do not break these totals out per building, so this registry records them as regional context rather than facts specific to the SPC1A building, and treats the Boolean Drive address, drawn from OpenStreetMap's reverse-geocoded coordinates, as the best currently available location detail for this structure pending a county assessor parcel lookup.

reading.body:
SPC1A, which opened in November 2019 as the first building of Google's Clarksville-Montgomery County campus, is Google's first data center facility in Tennessee. Google does not publish megawatt capacity at the individual building level, so the power this structure draws from the grid remains unknown; the campus overall is tied to a 413-megawatt renewable energy purchase agreement with the Tennessee Valley Authority sourced from solar farms across Tennessee and Alabama, one of the larger corporate renewable deals TVA has signed. The facility itself has no published capacity figure among the four Tennessee data center buildings with disclosed power output tracked by this site.

Among 24 mapped data center facilities in Tennessee, this building ranks fifth by published megawatt capacity, though it has none published. The state's four facilities with disclosed capacity total 12.13 megawatts, a figure that reflects only the few operators who publish individual site output; most mapped facilities in Tennessee, like this one, report no power consumption figure to the public.

Google's Tennessee investment since 2018 totals more than $6 billion under its current economic-impact methodology, which bundles data center construction with server and networking capital expenditure rather than isolating either, and the company reports this generated $11.4 billion of economic activity for Tennessee in 2025. Google does not break these figures out by building, so the contribution or power demand of SPC1A alone cannot be derived from published data.
